# Migration

| Guide                                   | For you if…                                                               |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [from-0.x.md](./from-0.x.md) _[How-to]_ | You use `@fathym/ioc` 0.0.x (up to 0.0.36) or 0.1.x and are moving to 1.0 |

The guide starts with a table of old and new calls, then explains each change.

From 1.0, breaking changes only come in major releases, each with its own guide here. The
[versioning and support policy](../policy.md) says what counts as breaking and how long a
deprecated API keeps working.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fathym/ioc/main/docs/migration/from-0.x.md (Migrating from 0.x to 1.0)

# Migrating from 0.x to 1.0

> **Goal:** Move code written for `@fathym/ioc` 0.0.x (up to 0.0.36) or 0.1.x to 1.0, and know
> exactly what behaves differently.

**Keys don't change.** A 1.0 token is `Symbol.for(name)`, as 0.x keys were, so `IoCToken('Db')`
and a `Symbol.for('Db')` key in code you haven't migrated yet are the same key. Most changes are
mechanical: explicit registration methods, no modes to configure, and modules instead of copying
containers. The compiler finds most of them.

A 1.0 container and a 0.x container are different classes and don't share registrations, so
every package that shares one container moves to 1.0 in the same release.

## Old call → new call

Rows marked _0.0.x_ only apply when you come from 0.0.x; rows marked _0.1_ only from 0.1.

| 0.x                                                                  | 1.0                                                                            | Notes                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ioc.Register(Clock)`, `Register(Clock, { Lifetime })`               | `ioc.RegisterClass(Clock, { Lifetime })`                                       | Add `Deps` when the constructor takes parameters          |
| `Register(PgDb, { Type: sym })`                                      | `RegisterClass(PgDb, { Type: $Db })`                                           | The class must satisfy the token's type                   |
| `Register(Cache, (c) => …)`, `Register(sym, (c) => …)`               | `RegisterFactory(Cache, (c) => …)`, `RegisterFactory($Token, (c) => …)`        |                                                           |
| `const remove = Register(…); remove()` _0.0.x_                       | `Unregister(key, name?)`                                                       | Registration methods return the container, for chaining   |
| `ioc.Symbol('Db')`, `Symbol.for('Db')`                               | `export const $Db = IoCToken<Db, 'Db'>('Db')`                                  | The same key, now typed                                   |
| String keys (`Resolve('Db')`)                                        | A token                                                                        | Throws `IOC_INVALID_KEY`                                  |
| `Resolve<Db>(sym)`, `TryResolve<T>`, `ResolveAll<T>`                 | `Resolve($Db)`: the type comes from the key                                    | An explicit type argument no longer compiles              |
| Registering a key and name again (last one wins)                     | `{ Replace: true }` on the replacement, or `{ Default: true }` on the default  | Otherwise throws `IOC_DUPLICATE_REGISTRATION`             |
| `{ Lazy: true }`, `LazyByDefault: true`                              | Remove them                                                                    | Everything is built on first resolve                      |
| `{ Lazy: false }`, eager singletons (the 0.0.x default)              | `await ioc.Activate()` at startup                                              | Builds every singleton, reports every failure             |
| `new IoCContainer({ Strict: true })`, `IoCContainer.Create()`        | `new IoCContainer()`                                                           | Always strict                                             |
| `PendingTimeoutMs` unset (wait forever)                              | 30 000 ms by default; `PendingTimeoutMs: 0` to wait forever                    | Also bounds `OnStart`, `OnStop` and disposers             |
| `AsyncContext: …` _0.1_                                              | Remove it; resolve through the factory's `ioc`                                 | [Cycles](#cycles)                                         |
| `Diagnostics: (d) => …` _0.1_                                        | Remove it                                                                      |                                                           |
| `await ioc.Start()` building every singleton _0.1_                   | `await ioc.Start(); await ioc.Activate();`                                     | `Start()` validates and starts modules; it builds nothing |
| `IoCKeyCollisionError`, `IOC_KEY_COLLISION` _0.1_                    | Remove it                                                                      | Tokens are names; a name is one key by design             |
| `Describe()` levels, observed deps, build state _0.1_                | `Describe()` lists registrations and modules only                              |                                                           |
| `source.CopyTo(target)`                                              | A module: `target.Use(SourceModule)`; or a child scope: `source.CreateScope()` | [Modules instead of CopyTo](#modules-instead-of-copyto)   |
| `ModuleFromContainer('Plugin', pluginIoc, { Defaults: true })` _0.1_ | The plugin exports an `IoCModule` whose registrations use `Default: true`      |                                                           |
| `RegisterDirect` / `ResolveDirect`                                   | `RegisterValue` / `Resolve`                                                    |                                                           |
| `ioc.services`, `ioc.symbols`                                        | `ioc.Describe()`, `ioc.Names(key)`, `ioc.Has(key)`                             |                                                           |
| `CreateScope({ Level })`, `ScopeLevel` _0.1_                         | `CreateScope()`; register per-level services on the scope that owns them       | [Scopes](#scopes)                                         |
| `Decorate(key, (inner) => …)` _0.1_                                  | Register the inner service under a name and wrap it in a factory               | [Decorate, IoCLazy, IoCAll](#decorate-ioclazy-iocall)     |
| `IoCLazy`/`IoCAll` in `ResolveRecord` _0.1_                          | Resolve those entries separately, or with a factory                            | [Decorate, IoCLazy, IoCAll](#decorate-ioclazy-iocall)     |
| `IoCLazy($X)` in `Deps` _0.1_                                        | A factory that keeps `ioc` and calls `ioc.Resolve($X)` later                   | [Decorate, IoCLazy, IoCAll](#decorate-ioclazy-iocall)     |
| `IoCAll($X)` in `Deps` _0.1_                                         | A factory that calls `await ioc.ResolveAll($X)`                                | [Decorate, IoCLazy, IoCAll](#decorate-ioclazy-iocall)     |
| `err.Symbol` on `IoCServiceNotFoundError`                            | `err.Key` (the token name or class name)                                       |                                                           |
| Matching messages (`No Service for symbol '…'`)                      | `isIoCError(err, 'IOC_SERVICE_NOT_FOUND')`                                     | Match on codes, not messages                              |

A typical composition root, after the change:

```ts
import { IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '@fathym/ioc';

interface Db {
  url: string;
}

export const $Db = IoCToken<Db, 'Db'>('Db'); // was: ioc.Symbol('Db')

class Clock {
  public now = () => Date.now();
}

class Notes {
  constructor(public db: Db, public clock: Clock) {}
}

const ioc = new IoCContainer() // was: IoCContainer.Create() or { Strict: true }
  .RegisterClass(Clock) // was: ioc.Register(Clock)
  .RegisterFactory($Db, () => ({ url: 'kv://local' })) // was: ioc.Register($Db, …)
  .RegisterClass(Notes, { Deps: [$Db, Clock] });

ioc.Validate(); // the wiring is sound
await ioc.Activate(); // build every singleton now (0.0.x did this by default)

console.log((await ioc.Resolve(Notes)).db.url); // kv://local

await ioc.Dispose();
```

## Behavior changes

### Registering twice throws

**0.x:** a second registration of the same key and name replaced the first, silently.

**1.0:** it throws `IoCDuplicateRegistrationError` unless it says `Replace: true`, or the first
was registered with `Default: true`. Frameworks register their replaceable services with
`Default: true`, and the application registers its own without any flag, before or after. The
exact rules are under [defaults](../reference/api.md#defaults).

```ts
import { IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '@fathym/ioc';

const $Greeting = IoCToken<string, 'Greeting'>('Greeting');

const ioc = new IoCContainer()
  .RegisterValue($Greeting, 'hello from the framework', { Default: true })
  .RegisterValue($Greeting, 'hello from the app'); // the default yields

console.log(await ioc.Resolve($Greeting)); // hello from the app
```

### Built on first resolve

**0.0.x** built singletons when they were registered. **1.0** builds a service the first time it
is resolved. Call `await ioc.Activate()` at startup to build every singleton now, so a broken
service fails the boot instead of the first request; it throws one `IoCActivationError` naming
every service that failed. `Start()` validates and starts modules, but builds nothing.

### Timeouts

A `Resolve`, a module's `OnStart`/`OnStop`, or a disposer still pending after 30 seconds fails
with `IoCResolveTimeoutError` instead of hanging. Raise it with
`new IoCContainer({ PendingTimeoutMs: 60_000 })`, or turn it off with `0`.

### Class keys are the class

**0.x** keyed a class by its name, so two different classes named `Config` could resolve each
other's registrations. **1.0** keys a class by the class itself. Tokens are still names.

### Cycles

A factory should resolve through the `ioc` it receives: then a cycle throws
`IoCCircularDependencyError` at once, naming the path. A cycle through a container captured in a
closure, after an `await`, can't be seen; it fails at the pending timeout instead.

### Modules instead of CopyTo

`CopyTo` copied one container's registrations into another. In 1.0 a package exports a module,
and the host adds it with `Use()`. A module lists the modules it builds on in `Requires`; they are
added first, once. `Start()` runs each module's `OnStart` in that order; if one fails, the
started modules are stopped again and `Start()` can be retried. `Dispose()` runs `OnStop` in
reverse.

```ts
import { IoCContainer, type IoCModule, IoCToken } from '@fathym/ioc';

const $Url = IoCToken<string, 'Url'>('Url');

// Was: a plugin container, copied into the host with CopyTo.
export const PluginModule: IoCModule = {
  Name: 'Plugin',
  Register: (ioc) => ioc.RegisterValue($Url, 'kv://plugin', { Default: true }),
  OnStart: () => console.log('plugin started'),
};

await using host = new IoCContainer().Use(PluginModule);

await host.Start(); // plugin started

console.log(await host.Resolve($Url)); // kv://plugin
```

### Scopes

`CreateScope()` makes a child container: `scoped` services get one instance per scope, and
registrations made on the scope override the parent's for that scope. Nested scopes work, but
there are no named levels: register a service on the scope that should own it (a tenant scope, a
request scope inside it). Disposing a container now disposes its live scopes too, and every
instance it built, in reverse order.

### Decorate, IoCLazy, IoCAll

0.1 had three dependency helpers that 1.0 leaves out. Each has a short replacement:

```ts
import { IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '@fathym/ioc';

interface Mailer {
  send(to: string): string;
}

const $Mailer = IoCToken<Mailer, 'Mailer'>('Mailer');
const $Handler = IoCToken<(path: string) => string, 'Handler'>('Handler');

class Signup {
  constructor(private mailer: () => Promise<Mailer>) {}

  async welcome(to: string) {
    return (await this.mailer()).send(to);
  }
}

class Router {
  constructor(public handlers: ((path: string) => string)[]) {}
}

const ioc = new IoCContainer()
  // Decorate: register the inner service under a name, and wrap it as the default.
  .RegisterValue($Mailer, { send: (to) => `sent to ${to}` }, { Name: 'inner' })
  .RegisterFactory($Mailer, async (c) => {
    const inner = await c.Resolve($Mailer, 'inner');

    return { send: (to) => inner.send(to).toUpperCase() };
  })
  // IoCLazy: keep the factory's ioc and resolve later.
  .RegisterFactory(Signup, (c) => new Signup(() => c.Resolve($Mailer)))
  // IoCAll: resolve every named registration in the factory.
  .RegisterValue($Handler, (p) => `api:${p}`, { Name: 'api' })
  .RegisterFactory(Router, async (c) => new Router(await c.ResolveAll($Handler)));

console.log(await (await ioc.Resolve(Signup)).welcome('ada')); // SENT TO ADA
console.log((await ioc.Resolve(Router)).handlers.length); // 1
```

`Validate()` doesn't see what a factory resolves in its body, only declared `Deps`.

## Checklist for a dependent repository

1. **Find what changes.** Search for `Register(`, `.Symbol(`, `CopyTo`, `ModuleFromContainer`,
   `RegisterDirect`, `ResolveDirect`, `.services`, `.symbols`, `Strict`, `IoCContainer.Create`,
   `Lazy`, `Diagnostics`, `AsyncContext`, `Level:`, `ScopeLevel`, `Decorate`, `IoCLazy`,
   `IoCAll`, `Resolve<` and `.Symbol` on errors.
2. **Type the keys.** Replace `ioc.Symbol('X')` and bare `Symbol.for('X')` with
   `IoCToken<T, 'X'>('X')`, exported from the package that owns the service. The name stays the
   same, so code you haven't migrated yet keeps finding it.
3. **Bump the dependency** to `jsr:@fathym/ioc@^1.0.0` (Node.js and Bun: `npx jsr add @fathym/ioc@^1.0.0`) in every
   package that shares a container, in the same release.
4. **Replace the calls** using [the table](#old-call--new-call), then run `deno check` and fix
   what it reports: explicit `Resolve<T>` arguments, string keys, `Deps` order.
5. **Make intended replacements explicit** with `Replace: true`, and framework defaults with
   `Default: true`.
6. **Move `CopyTo` and plugin containers to modules**, and `OnInit`/`OnDestroy` hooks to
   `OnStart`/`OnStop`.
7. **Start and stop through the container.** Call `await ioc.Start()` at boot (and
   `await ioc.Activate()` if you want every singleton built then), and `await ioc.Dispose()` (or
   `await using`) at shutdown, including on signals. Check that the 30-second pending timeout
   fits your slowest step.
8. **Add a wiring test** that calls `Validate()` on the real container.
9. **Match errors by code** with `isIoCError(err, code)` instead of their messages.
10. **Run the test suite** on every runtime you ship to (Node.js 20 or later, Bun, Deno), then
    release with a major version bump and a changelog entry that points your users here.

# Examples

Each example is a complete program that shows one idea. CI runs every one of them
(`tests/docs/examples.tests.ts`), so they always work with the current code.

Run any of them from the repository root:

```sh
deno run -A examples/basic.ts
deno test -A examples/testing-overrides.test.ts
```

> **Note:** These import from `../mod.ts` so they run against the source in this repository. In
> your own project, import from `@fathym/ioc` instead.

| Example                                                  | Shows                                                                                                                     | Read more                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [basic.ts](./basic.ts)                                   | Values, classes, declared `Deps`, `Validate()`, singletons                                                                | [first-container.md](../docs/getting-started/first-container.md)       |
| [async-services.ts](./async-services.ts)                 | Deno KV from an async factory, a flaky client that succeeds on retry, `Activate()`, `Dispose()`                           | [async-services.md](../docs/getting-started/async-services.md)         |
| [per-request-server.ts](./per-request-server.ts)         | An HTTP app: `Start()` and `Activate()`, a scope per request, disposable services, graceful shutdown                      | [per-request-scopes.md](../docs/getting-started/per-request-scopes.md) |
| [testing-overrides.test.ts](./testing-overrides.test.ts) | Validating the real module, then faking one dependency with `Override()`                                                  | [testing-your-app.md](../docs/getting-started/testing-your-app.md)     |
| [plugins.ts](./plugins.ts)                               | Named implementations, `ResolveAll`, `TryResolve`, `Has`                                                                  | [api.md](../docs/reference/api.md)                                     |
| [typed-container.ts](./typed-container.ts)               | `Typed()` chains, `DefineModule` with `Needs` checked by `Use()`, `Expect` for a per-request key                          | [api.md](../docs/reference/api.md)                                     |
| [modules-lifecycle.ts](./modules-lifecycle.ts)           | Typed modules, a default the app replaces, a failed `Start()` that stops what started and is retried, `OnStop` on dispose | [api.md](../docs/reference/api.md)                                     |

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fathym/ioc/main/examples/async-services.ts

```ts
/**
 * Async services: a Deno KV opened by an async factory, a flaky remote client that succeeds on retry, startup
 * activation and disposal.
 *
 * Run: deno run --unstable-kv examples/async-services.ts
 */
import { IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '../mod.ts';

interface RemoteConfig {
  featureFlags: string[];
}

const $RemoteConfig = IoCToken<RemoteConfig, 'RemoteConfig'>('RemoteConfig');

let configAttempts = 0;

/** Pretends to fetch configuration; the first call fails like a service that is still starting. */
async function fetchRemoteConfig(): Promise<RemoteConfig> {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5));

  if (++configAttempts === 1) throw new Error('config service not ready');

  return { featureFlags: ['notes-v2'] };
}

const ioc = new IoCContainer();

// Nothing is built at registration.
ioc.RegisterFactory(Deno.Kv, () => Deno.openKv(':memory:'));
ioc.RegisterFactory($RemoteConfig, fetchRemoteConfig);

// Activate builds every singleton now and reports all failures together.
try {
  await ioc.Activate();
} catch (err) {
  console.log(`Startup attempt failed: ${(err as AggregateError).message}`);
}

// Failed creations are not cached, so activating again retries only what failed.
await ioc.Activate();

const [kv, config] = await Promise.all([ioc.Resolve(Deno.Kv), ioc.Resolve($RemoteConfig)]);

await kv.set(['flags'], config.featureFlags);

console.log('Flags in KV:', (await kv.get<string[]>(['flags'])).value);

await ioc.Dispose(); // closes the KV connection

if (configAttempts !== 2) throw new Error(`expected 2 attempts, got ${configAttempts}`);
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fathym/ioc/main/examples/basic.ts

```ts
/**
 * Basic registration and resolution: a value, classes and declared dependencies.
 *
 * Run: deno run examples/basic.ts
 */
import { IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '../mod.ts';

const $AppName = IoCToken<string, 'AppName'>('AppName');

class Clock {
  public now(): Date {
    return new Date();
  }
}

class Greeter {
  constructor(private clock: Clock, private appName: string) {}

  public greet(name: string): string {
    return `[${this.appName} @ ${this.clock.now().toISOString()}] Hello, ${name}!`;
  }
}

const ioc = new IoCContainer();

ioc.RegisterValue($AppName, 'Basic example');
ioc.RegisterClass(Clock);
ioc.RegisterClass(Greeter, { Deps: [Clock, $AppName] });

ioc.Validate();

const greeter = await ioc.Resolve(Greeter);

console.log(greeter.greet('world'));

if ((await ioc.Resolve(Greeter)) !== greeter) throw new Error('expected a singleton');
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fathym/ioc/main/examples/modules-lifecycle.ts

```ts
/**
 * Modules and lifecycle: typed modules with DefineModule, Requires deciding the start order, a
 * framework default the app replaces, a failed Start() that stops what started and is retried,
 * and Dispose() stopping the modules in reverse.
 *
 * Run: deno run examples/modules-lifecycle.ts
 */
import { DefineModule, IoCContainer, IoCToken, isIoCError } from '../mod.ts';

const $DbUrl = IoCToken<string, 'example/DbUrl'>('example/DbUrl');

const events: string[] = [];

function log(event: string): void {
  events.push(event);
  console.log(`  ${event}`);
}

class Db {
  public open = false;

  constructor(public url: string) {}

  [Symbol.asyncDispose](): Promise<void> {
    log(`db disposed (${this.url})`);
    return Promise.resolve();
  }
}

class MemoryCache {
  public readonly entries = new Map<string, string>();
}

// A default: the module says "the app may replace this".
const Config = DefineModule({
  Name: 'Config',
  Register: (ioc) => ioc.RegisterValue($DbUrl, 'postgres://localhost/app', { Default: true }),
});

const Database = DefineModule({
  Name: 'Database',
  Requires: [Config], // added and started before Database
  Register: (ioc) => ioc.RegisterClass(Db, { Deps: [$DbUrl] }), // $DbUrl is typed in from Config
  OnStart: async (ioc) => {
    (await ioc.Resolve(Db)).open = true;
    log('database connected');
  },
  OnStop: async (ioc) => {
    (await ioc.Resolve(Db)).open = false;
    log('database drained');
  },
});

const Cache = DefineModule({
  Name: 'Cache',
  Register: (ioc) => ioc.RegisterClass(MemoryCache),
  OnStart: () => log('cache warmed'),
  OnStop: () => log('cache flushed'),
});

let portFree = false;

const Server = DefineModule({
  Name: 'Server',
  Requires: [Database, Cache],
  Register: () => {},
  OnStart: () => {
    if (!portFree) throw new Error('port 8080 in use');
    log('server listening');
  },
  OnStop: () => log('server closed'),
});

{
  await using ioc = new IoCContainer()
    .Typed()
    .Use(Server) // adds Config, Database, Cache, then Server
    .RegisterValue($DbUrl, 'postgres://db.internal/app'); // replaces Config's default

  console.log(`Start order: ${ioc.Describe().Modules.map((m) => m.Name).join(', ')}`);

  console.log('First start:');

  try {
    await ioc.Start();
  } catch (err) {
    if (!isIoCError(err, 'IOC_START_FAILED')) throw err;
    console.log(`  ${err.message}; state is back to '${ioc.State}'`);
  }

  portFree = true;

  console.log('Second start:');

  await ioc.Start();

  const db = await ioc.Resolve(Db);

  if (db.url !== 'postgres://db.internal/app' || !db.open) throw new Error('unexpected Db');

  console.log('Shutdown:');
} // `await using` disposes the container here: modules stop in reverse, then instances

const expected = [
  // First start: Server fails, so the modules that started are stopped again, in reverse.
  'database connected',
  'cache warmed',
  'cache flushed',
  'database drained',
  // Second start.
  'database connected',
  'cache warmed',
  'server listening',
  // Dispose().
  'server closed',
  'cache flushed',
  'database drained',
  'db disposed (postgres://db.internal/app)',
];

if (events.join('|') !== expected.join('|')) throw new Error(`unexpected order: ${events}`);
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fathym/ioc/main/examples/per-request-server.ts

```ts
/**
 * A realistic end-to-end app: an HTTP server where every request gets its own scope, request
 * value and scoped services, with graceful shutdown that disposes the root container.
 *
 * Run: deno run -A --unstable-kv examples/per-request-server.ts
 * (it starts on a random port, sends itself three requests, prints the results and exits)
 */
import { IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '../mod.ts';

const $Request = IoCToken<Request, 'Request'>('Request');

abstract class NotesStore {
  public abstract add(text: string): Promise<void>;
  public abstract count(): Promise<number>;
}

class KvNotesStore extends NotesStore {
  constructor(private kv: Deno.Kv) {
    super();
  }

  public async add(text: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.kv.set(['notes', crypto.randomUUID()], text);
  }

  public async count(): Promise<number> {
    let n = 0;
    for await (const _ of this.kv.list({ prefix: ['notes'] })) n++;
    return n;
  }
}

/** One per request: the scope disposes it when the response is done. */
class RequestLog implements Disposable {
  public static closed = 0;

  public readonly id = crypto.randomUUID().slice(0, 8);

  public [Symbol.dispose](): void {
    RequestLog.closed++;
  }
}

class NotesHandler {
  constructor(private req: Request, private log: RequestLog, private store: NotesStore) {}

  public async handle(): Promise<Response> {
    if (this.req.method === 'POST') await this.store.add(await this.req.text());

    return Response.json({ request: this.log.id, notes: await this.store.count() });
  }
}

// Composition root.
const ioc = new IoCContainer();

ioc.RegisterFactory(Deno.Kv, () => Deno.openKv(':memory:'));
ioc.RegisterFactory(NotesStore, (_ioc, kv) => new KvNotesStore(kv), { Deps: [Deno.Kv] });
ioc.Expect($Request); // registered on each request's scope, below
ioc.RegisterClass(RequestLog, { Lifetime: 'scoped' });
ioc.RegisterClass(NotesHandler, {
  Deps: [$Request, RequestLog, NotesStore],
  Lifetime: 'transient',
});

await ioc.Start(); // validates the wiring
await ioc.Activate(); // opens KV now, so a bad setup fails at startup

const server = Deno.serve({ port: 0, onListen() {} }, async (req) => {
  await using scope = ioc.CreateScope();

  scope.RegisterValue($Request, req);

  return await (await scope.Resolve(NotesHandler)).handle();
});

const url = `http://localhost:${server.addr.port}/notes`;

for (const body of ['Buy milk', 'Call Ada']) {
  console.log(await (await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body })).json());
}

console.log(await (await fetch(url)).json());

await server.shutdown();
await ioc.Dispose(); // closes KV

if (RequestLog.closed !== 3) {
  throw new Error(`expected 3 disposed request logs, got ${RequestLog.closed}`);
}
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fathym/ioc/main/examples/plugins.ts

```ts
/**
 * Plugins: several named implementations of one key, collected with ResolveAll and picked by
 * name with TryResolve.
 *
 * Run: deno run examples/plugins.ts
 */
import { IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '../mod.ts';

interface Exporter {
  readonly format: string;
  export(rows: string[]): string;
}

const $Exporter = IoCToken<Exporter, 'Exporter'>('Exporter');

const ioc = new IoCContainer();

ioc.RegisterValue($Exporter, { format: 'csv', export: (rows) => rows.join(',') }, { Name: 'csv' });
ioc.RegisterValue($Exporter, { format: 'json', export: (rows) => JSON.stringify(rows) }, {
  Name: 'json',
});
ioc.RegisterValue($Exporter, { format: 'lines', export: (rows) => rows.join('\n') }, {
  Name: 'lines',
});

const all = await ioc.ResolveAll($Exporter);

console.log('Available formats:', all.map((e) => e.format).join(', '));

const requested = 'json';
const exporter = await ioc.TryResolve($Exporter, requested);

if (!exporter) throw new Error(`no exporter for ${requested}`);

console.log(exporter.export(['a', 'b']));

console.log('Has xml?', ioc.Has($Exporter, 'xml'));
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fathym/ioc/main/examples/testing-overrides.test.ts

```ts
/**
 * Testing with overrides: validate the real app module, fake one dependency with `Override()`,
 * and put the original back with the function `Override()` returns.
 *
 * Run: deno test examples/testing-overrides.test.ts
 */
import { assertEquals, assertRejects } from 'jsr:@std/assert@1.0.16';
import { DefineModule, IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '../mod.ts';

interface Mailer {
  send(to: string, subject: string): Promise<void>;
}

const $Mailer = IoCToken<Mailer, 'example/Mailer'>('example/Mailer');

class SignupService {
  constructor(private mailer: Mailer) {}

  public async signUp(email: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.mailer.send(email.toLowerCase(), 'Welcome!');
  }
}

/** The production wiring, shared by the app and the tests. */
const App = DefineModule({
  Name: 'App',
  Register: (ioc) =>
    ioc
      .RegisterFactory($Mailer, () => ({
        send: () => Promise.reject(new Error('no SMTP server in tests')),
      }))
      .RegisterClass(SignupService, { Deps: [$Mailer], Lifetime: 'transient' }),
});

Deno.test('the production wiring is valid', () => {
  new IoCContainer().Use(App).Validate();
});

Deno.test('signUp sends a welcome mail to the normalized address', async () => {
  await using ioc = new IoCContainer().Use(App);

  const sent: string[] = [];

  // Override before resolving the services that use it.
  ioc.Override($Mailer, {
    send: (to, subject) => Promise.resolve(void sent.push(`${to}: ${subject}`)),
  });

  await (await ioc.Resolve(SignupService)).signUp('Ada@Example.com');

  assertEquals(sent, ['ada@example.com: Welcome!']);
});

Deno.test('the function Override() returns puts the original back', async () => {
  await using ioc = new IoCContainer().Use(App); // imagine it shared by several tests

  const restore = ioc.Override($Mailer, { send: () => Promise.resolve() });

  await (await ioc.Resolve(SignupService)).signUp('ada@example.com'); // the fake: no error

  restore();

  await assertRejects(
    async () => await (await ioc.Resolve(SignupService)).signUp('ada@example.com'),
    Error,
    'no SMTP server in tests',
  );
});
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fathym/ioc/main/examples/typed-container.ts

```ts
/**
 * Typed containers: `Typed()` plus chained registrations, so `Deps` may only name what's already
 * registered. Feature modules made with `DefineModule` state the keys they need, `Use()` checks
 * them, and a per-request key is declared with `Expect`.
 *
 * Run: deno run examples/typed-container.ts
 */
import { DefineModule, IoCContainer, IoCToken } from '../mod.ts';

interface Db {
  query(sql: string): string[];
}

const $Db = IoCToken<Db, 'Db'>('Db');
const $Table = IoCToken<string, 'Table'>('Table');
const $Request = IoCToken<Request, 'Request'>('Request');

class NotesRepo {
  constructor(public db: Db, public table: string) {}

  public list(): string[] {
    return this.db.query(`select * from ${this.table}`);
  }
}

class NotesHandler {
  constructor(public repo: NotesRepo, public req: Request) {}

  public handle(): string {
    return `${new URL(this.req.url).pathname}: ${this.repo.list().join(', ')}`;
  }
}

// data.ts: provides $Db and nothing else.
const Data = DefineModule({
  Name: 'Data',
  Register: (ioc) => ioc.RegisterValue($Db, { query: (sql) => [`ran "${sql}"`] }),
});

// notes.ts: needs $Db and $Request from someone else. Inside Register, Deps may name those,
// plus what this chain registered above.
const Notes = DefineModule({
  Name: 'Notes',
  Needs: [$Db, $Request],
  Register: (ioc) =>
    ioc
      .RegisterValue($Table, 'notes')
      .RegisterClass(NotesRepo, { Deps: [$Db, $Table] })
      .RegisterClass(NotesHandler, { Deps: [NotesRepo, $Request], Lifetime: 'transient' }),
});

// main.ts: drop `.Use(Data)` or `.Expect($Request)` and the `.Use(Notes)` line won't compile.
const ioc = new IoCContainer()
  .Typed()
  .Expect($Request) // registered on each request's scope
  .Use(Data)
  .Use(Notes);

ioc.Validate();

await using scope = ioc.CreateScope();

scope.RegisterValue($Request, new Request('http://localhost/notes'));

const output = (await scope.Resolve(NotesHandler)).handle();

console.log(output); // /notes: ran "select * from notes"

if (output !== '/notes: ran "select * from notes"') throw new Error(`unexpected: ${output}`);
```
